purpose: Run a program in newly created namespaces. The userspace front-end to the unshare(2) syscall family. The 'create a fresh container-like environment without a runtime' tool — sysadmins use it to debug namespace behavior, mount/unmount inside an isolated mountns, or test a program's response to fresh PID/network namespaces. Without --fork, the new PID namespace's pid 1 is unshare itself; with --fork, unshare clones a child to be pid 1 (almost always what you want for --pid). util-linux package; ships with every modern distro.

flags.name: -i, --ipc
flags.doc: Create a new IPC namespace. If file given, persist the namespace via bind-mount on file.

flags.name: -m, --mount
flags.doc: Create a new mount namespace. Auto-sets propagation to private (override with --propagation unchanged). The mount-point hosting the persist-file must NOT be MS_SHARED.

flags.name: -n, --net
flags.doc: Create a new network namespace. Independent IPv4/IPv6 stacks, routes, firewall, /proc/net, /sys/class/net, sockets.

flags.name: -p, --pid
flags.doc: Create a new PID namespace for children. Combine with --fork so unshare itself doesn't become pid 1 of the new namespace.

flags.name: -u, --uts
flags.doc: Create a new UTS namespace. Hostname/domainname changes don't leak to the host.

flags.name: -U, --user
flags.doc: Create a new user namespace. Useful with --map-root-user to get root inside without being root outside.

flags.name: -C, --cgroup
flags.doc: Create a new cgroup namespace. The new process sees its cgroup as root in /proc/self/cgroup.

flags.name: -T, --time
flags.doc: Create a new time namespace. CLOCK_MONOTONIC/CLOCK_BOOTTIME offsets via /proc/self/timens_offsets. Requires kernel 5.6+.

flags.name: -f, --fork
flags.doc: fork() before launching the program — child becomes pid 1 of the new PID namespace, unshare exits when child does.

flags.name: --mount-proc
flags.doc: Just before running the program, mount procfs at mountpoint (default /proc) inside the new mount namespace. Required when entering a new --pid namespace, otherwise /proc still shows host PIDs.

flags.name: --kill-child
flags.doc: Send signame (default SIGKILL) to the child if unshare's parent process dies. PR_SET_PDEATHSIG semantics.

flags.name: -r, --map-root-user
flags.doc: Map the calling user/group to 0/0 in the new user namespace. Shorthand for the common rootless-debugging pattern.

flags.name: --map-current-user
flags.doc: Map the calling user/group to themselves (1:1) in the new user namespace. Useful for unprivileged setups that want to keep an unprivileged identity.

flags.name: --map-user
flags.doc: Map current user to <uid|name> in new userns. Companion --map-group=<gid|name>.

flags.name: --map-users
flags.doc: Add a UID-mapping range to /proc/self/uid_map (requires newuidmap if non-root).

flags.name: --map-groups
flags.doc: Add a GID-mapping range to /proc/self/gid_map (requires newgidmap if non-root).

flags.name: --keep-caps
flags.doc: Set PR_SET_KEEPCAPS so the calling thread retains its capabilities across the upcoming setuid(0) when entering a userns. Otherwise caps reset on UID change.

flags.name: --setgroups
flags.doc: Permit or deny setgroups(2) inside the new user namespace. Writing 'deny' to /proc/self/setgroups is required before unprivileged GID mapping; 'allow' requires CAP_SETGID in parent userns.

flags.name: --propagation
flags.doc: Mount-propagation type for the new mount namespace's root mount. Default 'private' (since v2.27).

flags.name: -R, --root
flags.doc: chroot to dir before running the program (after namespace setup).

flags.name: -w, --wd
flags.doc: chdir to dir before running the program.

examples.expected_output: a bash where `id` reports uid=0 root and `ps` shows only bash + ps
examples.scenario: Quick rootless container-like shell for testing — userns + pidns isolation without docker.

examples.expected_output: a fresh network namespace with only loopback (and no IP); ip link prints just `lo`
examples.scenario: Inspect what a brand-new netns looks like (useful for debugging container network setup).

examples.expected_output: a bash whose mounts are private to itself; mount/umount don't affect host
examples.scenario: Test a tricky mount sequence (overlayfs, bind-mount tree) without polluting the host's mount table.

purpose: Enter one or more namespaces of an existing process and run a command inside. The userspace front-end to setns(2). The fundamental 'attach to a running container's namespaces' tool — `docker exec` and `kubectl exec` are layered atop this primitive (via the runtime). Without --target, can take individual --<ns>=<file> options pointing to /proc/<pid>/ns/* magic links or persisted bind-mounts.

flags.name: -t, --target
flags.doc: PID of the process whose namespaces will be entered. Combine with -a or per-namespace flags.

flags.name: -a, --all
flags.doc: Enter ALL namespaces of the target. Convenient shorthand for `-mUipnCu`.

flags.name: -m, --mount
flags.doc: Enter the target's mount namespace (or the namespace identified by file).

flags.name: -u, --uts
flags.doc: Enter UTS namespace.

flags.name: -i, --ipc
flags.doc: Enter IPC namespace.

flags.name: -n, --net
flags.doc: Enter network namespace.

flags.name: -p, --pid
flags.doc: Enter PID namespace. Note: only affects the new program's children; nsenter itself remains in the original PID namespace until it execs.

flags.name: -C, --cgroup
flags.doc: Enter cgroup namespace.

flags.name: -U, --user
flags.doc: Enter user namespace. Must be done before joining other namespaces if cred change is required.

flags.name: -T, --time
flags.doc: Enter time namespace.

flags.name: -r, --root
flags.doc: chroot to the target's root (or to dir). Without arg, uses target's /proc/<pid>/root.

flags.name: -w, --wd
flags.doc: chdir to target's CWD or to the given dir.

flags.name: -F, --no-fork
flags.doc: Do not fork before exec — useful when entering only --user/--mount/--uts (no PID-ns) and you want nsenter's PID to be the entered-program's PID.

flags.name: -S, --setuid
flags.doc: Set UID via setuid(2) in the entered namespaces (after possible --root chroot).

flags.name: -G, --setgid
flags.doc: Set GID via setgid(2).

flags.name: --preserve-credentials
flags.doc: Don't change uid/gid when entering the user namespace (the default IS to drop privileges in the joined userns).

examples.expected_output: a bash inside container PID 12345's namespaces — /proc, hostname, net interfaces match the container
examples.scenario: Debug a running container from the host without docker exec — works even if dockerd is unhealthy.

examples.expected_output: the host's mount table (since pid 1 lives in the host mountns)
examples.scenario: From inside a privileged container with /proc bind-mounted, peek at the host's mount table.

examples.expected_output: routes inside the persisted netns named myns
examples.scenario: Inspect routing inside a persistent netns set up via `ip netns add myns`.

purpose: Move the current root filesystem to put_old and make new_root the new root. Userspace front-end to pivot_root(2). The 'switch the rootfs cleanly inside a mount namespace' tool — what container runtimes do during container start (after preparing new_root with the image's rootfs). Safer than chroot because once the old root is unmounted, escape via reusing chroot is impossible.

flags.name: -h, --help
flags.doc: Print help.

flags.name: -V, --version
flags.doc: Print version.

examples.invocation: unshare --mount sh -c 'mkdir /mnt/newroot && mount -t tmpfs none /mnt/newroot && mkdir /mnt/newroot/oldroot && pivot_root /mnt/newroot /mnt/newroot/oldroot'
examples.expected_output: new root is now the tmpfs; the old root is at /oldroot
examples.scenario: Demonstrate pivot_root mechanics in a private mount namespace without affecting host.

examples.invocation: # inside a container init: mount image rootfs at /newroot, then\npivot_root /newroot /newroot/oldroot && umount -l /oldroot
examples.expected_output: container's pid 1 sees / as the image rootfs; old (host) root is unreachable
examples.scenario: Standard container-runtime pivot pattern — ensures escape is impossible after the old root is lazy-unmounted.
